grants.title: GO8606: Remote Training Hubs Network: Central Australia Remote Training Hubs Grant - Round 3
grants.summary: The Australian Government is inviting organisations via a closed, non-competitive process to apply to deliver services under Program 2.1: Building Skills and Capability from February 2027 to 30 June 2028. The Central Australia Remote Training Hubs Grant, funded through the Remote Training Hubs Network measure, was announced by the Prime Minister on 13 February 2024, under the A Better, Safer Future for Central Australia (Central Australia Plan), to support the delivery of vocational education and training in up to 7 remote community clusters in Central Australia, through the provision of funding for capital assets or improvements, remote training hub coordination and mentoring and participant transport to 30 June 2028. This third round of the Central Australia Remote Training Hubs grant opportunity is open to The Plenty cluster only. The remaining community clusters will be invited to apply in subsequent grant round(s). The Central Australia Mobile Training Units (MTUs) Grant (ID GO7445) is linked to this grant opportunity. If successful, you will be required to work in partnership with the Registered Training Organisations (RTOs) delivering services via the MTUs.

grants.title: GO8341: Modernised Multicultural Grants Program: Infrastructure for Multicultural Communities
grants.summary: Assessment and notification of outcomes will be divided into 2 batches. The table below identifies the cut-off dates for each batch: Batch 1 - closes 4:00 pm AEST on 18 May 2026 - ID 2025-5201 - Closed Batch 2 - closes 4:00 pm AEDT on 12 November 2026 - ID 2026-6462 - Open. The Australian Government is inviting organisations through an open competitive process to apply to deliver community infrastructure under the Infrastructure for Multicultural Communities program from 2026–27. The Infrastructure for Multicultural Communities grant opportunity provides total funding of up to $41.6 million (GST exclusive) for construction, upgrade or extension of infrastructure. You can apply for one of 3 streams of grant funding based on the type of infrastructure project and amount of grant funding you require for the project. The grant opportunity is comprised of 2 funding opportunities, called batches. You can apply for funding in one batch. Batch 1 opens on 7 April 2026 and closes on 18 May 2026. Batch 2 opens on 18 May 2026 and closes on 12 November 2026. The following groups and projects will be prioritised for funding: new and emerging multicultural communities, as defined below projects focussed on achieving positive outcomes for multicultural women, multicultural LGBTIQA+ community members, and multicultural people with a disability. Co-contributions are required towards the value of your project and the minimum amount of co funding is determined by whether you are applying as a priority group/project or other. The objectives of the grant opportunity are to: deliver physical infrastructure to support multicultural communities connect and commune in a designated physical environment provide co-funding to deliver community-focussed infrastructure and amenities provide infrastructure and amenities that benefit the wider multicultural community by improving equity and social inclusion.

grants.title: GO8220: Saluting their Service Commemorative Grants Program 2026–27
grants.summary: Assessment and notification of outcomes will be into 2 batches. The table below identifies the cut-off dates for all 2 batches: Batch 1 - closes 9:00 PM AEST on 29 July 2026 - ID 2025-5415 - Closed Batch 2 - closes 9:00 PM AEDT 21 January 2027 - ID 2025-5416 - Open. The Australian Government is inviting eligible organisations to apply for grant funding under the Saluting Their Service Commemorative Grants Program (STS program). The objective of the STS Program is to commemorate the service and sacrifice of Australia’s service personnel who served in wars, conflicts and peace operations, including National Service personnel, and their families. The intended outcome of the STS Program is to provide funding for projects and activities that: promote appreciation and understanding of the experiences of service, and the role of service personnel preserve, add to the sum of knowledge on, or provide access to information about Australia’s wartime heritage. 1. Community Grants Grants up to $10,000 are available for projects and activities that: are focused on the local community commemorate the service and sacrifice of local community members are primarily accessed by the local community. 2. Major Grants Grants between $10,001 and $150,000 are available for major commemorative projects and activities that are significant from a national, state, territory and/or broader regional perspective. These projects may include the construction of new war or peace memorials where none currently exist, as well as additions to existing memorials. If your project relates to restoring or changing a memorial or other commemorative artefact, there may be heritage and conservation considerations.

grants.title: GO8507: Dementia Training Program
grants.summary: The Dementia Training Program (DTP), first established nationally in 2016, aims to strengthen the capability of Australia’s health and aged care workforce to provide high-quality, evidence-based dementia care. The purpose of this grant opportunity is to fund the delivery of accredited and non-accredited education, upskilling and professional development in dementia care. The delivery of DTP activities will reflect the emerging dementia, health and aged care landscape, including recent aged care reforms and increasing demand for services. DTP activities will: • Be aligned with a National Dementia Training and Education Standards Framework. • Expand experiential, immersive, peer mentoring and interprofessional training. • Adopt tailored approaches for diverse workforce groups and communities including for First Nations people, those from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds and people from regional, rural and remote locations. • Build organisational capability and leadership for high quality dementia care, including sustainable practice change. • Deliver key service elements responding to the Royal Commission into Aged Care Quality and Safety. There are two funding streams: Stream 1 aims to improve capability of health and aged care workers to provide high quality dementia care for non-Indigenous Australians, including people from diverse backgrounds. Stream 2 focuses on culturally safe, community-led dementia training for First Nations communities and workforces. NOTE: Please refer to the most recent Frequently Asked Questions (Version 4) published 2 September 2026. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8582: Embedding and Promoting the National Best Practice Framework for Early Childhood Intervention
grants.summary: This grant opportunity forms part of the Australian Government’s investment in the Thriving Kids program announced in the 2026-27 Federal Budget and supports activities that strengthened best practice early childhood intervention across Australia. The National Best Practice Framework for Early Childhood Intervention (the Framework) sets out what high-quality, evidence-informed early childhood intervention looks like for children under 9 years of age with developmental concerns, delay or disability, and their families. It provides guidance to services, practitioners and families on delivering and accessing effective, tailored supports, to enable participation in everyday life and achieve the best possible outcomes. The purpose of this grant opportunity is to promote and embed the Framework across the sector by improving awareness, capability and uptake of best practice early childhood intervention (ECI) approaches across workforce groups and the broader community including ECI practitioners, organisations, families, carers, kin and other stakeholders. This will contribute to improved quality, consistency and accessibility of ECI supports across Australia, supporting delivery of the objectives of the Thriving Kids National Model. The Department will engage University of Melbourne and Professionals and Researchers in Early Childhood Intervention (PRECI) to deliver activities to ECI practitioners and organisations, as well as families and communities, to use and apply the Framework consistently across Australia and promote best practice ECI approaches for the children and families they support. Note: Please see updated Attachment Pack – Version 2 published on 24 September 2026. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8439: Defence Strategic Policy Research Program
grants.summary: The Defence Strategic Policy Research Program grant opportunity will provide operating funding to the Australian strategic policy sector for up to five years, from 2027–28 to 2031–32. This grant opportunity was established to implement the government response to the 2024 Independent Review of Commonwealth funding for strategic policy work (the Varghese review). The grant opportunity is confined to activities that support the Australian Defence Force (or other defence purposes), with the majority of an organisation’s business-as-usual activities directed toward the annual national security policy research priorities, set by the Secretaries’ Committee on National Security (SCNS) and published by the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet. The objectives of the grant opportunity are to promote the development of Australia’s defence and national security policy and strategy by: informing and shaping debate through quality research, discussion fora, and other strategic policy work on Australian strategic and defence policy issues deepening public discussion on Australia’s strategic and defence policy choices strengthening engagement between Defence and the strategic policy sector. The intended outcomes of the grant opportunity are: published original, evidence-based strategic policy research development of new and emerging talent within the Australian strategic policy sector, promoting equitable and diverse participation, including with gender-diverse and/or First Nations-led organisations enhanced engagement with public and private sector experts, including outside metropolitan locations enriched professional development for Defence personnel (military and civilian).

grants.title: GO8578: Australia-Indonesia Institute Grants Program - 2026-27 Grant Round Guidelines
grants.summary: The Australia-Indonesia Institute (AII) Grant Program provides grants each year to develop, promote and strengthen understanding and engagement between Australia and Indonesia. The AII Grant Program’s objectives are to: increase public interest and understanding of Indonesia in Australia, and of the importance of the bilateral relationship, across a broad audience; increase Australians’ capability to effectively engage with Indonesia; and to develop partnerships, collaborations and people-to-people links in areas of shared interest in the bilateral and regional context. To deliver on its objectives, the focus of the annual program pivots from year to year. The 2026-27 grant opportunity will focus on Indonesian capability and language. Australia’s security, prosperity and economic future are intrinsically tied to our region. The 2026-27 Budget expanded funding for the Australia Indonesia Institute under the Implementing the Australia-Indonesia Treaty on Common Security (the Jakarta Treaty 2026) budget measure. The AII’s 2026-27 grant round will champion initiatives that explicitly aim to strengthen Australia’s national Indonesia capability. Indonesia capability refers to the knowledge, skills, experience, and networks that enable effective engagement with Indonesia. Priority will be given to projects that can demonstrate how they improve Australia’s ability to engage with Indonesia by building cultural understanding and knowledge, Indonesian language skills, and sustainable networks across community, schools and universities.

grants.title: GO8571: Visions of Australia - Round 23
grants.summary: The Visions of Australia Program provides funding to support the development and touring of quality exhibitions around Australia by Australian arts and cultural organisations. The objectives of the Visions of Australia Program are to: increase access for Australian audiences to exhibitions of quality Australian arts and cultural material, with a particular focus on touring to regional and remote Australia encourage partnerships between organisations such as museums and galleries, particularly collaboration across the collections sector, to form curatorial partnerships and where appropriate, access to mentoring and skills transfer opportunities. Program funding is delivered through two streams: Development: for the costs of planning and producing an exhibition to tour. This includes research and design Touring: for the costs to produce the exhibition and the costs to transport, install and dismantle the exhibition as well as deliver public programs. The Program delivers two funding rounds each year usually opening in February and September noting that the department is currently considering revising the Program Grant Opportunity structure to run one funding round per year from 2026-27. The Office for the Arts will be seeking views from stakeholders about which timing would best suit applicant organisations if only one round is held per year (ie either September 2026 or February 2027).The Minister for the Arts (or his delegate) approves funding under the Program Guidelines based on an assessment by the Department and independent assessors.

grants.title: GO8512: Aged Care Award Wages - Historical Leave Liabilities Increases - 1 August 2026
grants.summary: The purpose of this grant opportunity is to provide $12.033 million in 2026-27 in one-off funding to eligible registered providers to pay eligible registered and enrolled nurses working in aged care to take their leave entitlements at the increased wage rates effective from 1 August 2026 as a result of the FWC decision under the ACWVC only. This grant opportunity will only cover: • 1 August 2026 wage increases for eligible registered and enrolled nurses working in aged care. This grant opportunity recognises that accumulated leave liabilities for eligible registered and enrolled nurses working in aged care will have increased as a result of the FWC ACWVC decision that applied from 1 August 2026, and the associated cost to registered providers of aged care when these nurses take this leave will have increased. Eligible registered providers include those that provide one or more of the following Commonwealth funded aged care programs: • Residential Aged Care, • Support at Home Program, • Commonwealth Home Support Program (CHSP), • Transition Care Program, and / or • National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Flexible Aged Care Program (NATSIFACP). To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8583: Thriving Kids - Autism Community Engagement
grants.summary: The aim of the grant activity is to design, deliver and evaluate national engagement activities with the Autistic and autism community from January 2027 until June 2028, as part of the Thriving Kids initiative. Funding will be provided for a two-year period, with the potential to extend up to June 2031, subject to performance, program requirements and decisions of government. The grant aims to deliver meaningful outcomes for Autistic children, their families, carers and kin by: • Raising awareness and understanding of best practice for child development and available supports outside the NDIS, including Thriving Kids • Building skills and confidence of families, carers and kin of Autistic children • Collect and share feedback with governments, on how supports outside the NDIS, particularly Thriving Kids services are operating in practice and any areas for improvement. Design of this component will be agreed in conjunction with the Commonwealth and state and territory governments. Engagement activities are to be locally relevant, tailored to meet the needs of families, carers and kin with intersectional experiences, including, but not limited to, First Nations people, Culturally and Linguistically Diverse people, rural and remote communities and parents with disabilities. Overall, the grant seeks to support targeted engagement with the Autistic and autism community, so governments can design and implement supports that reflect lived experience, build confidence, and help children and families feel understood, included and supported. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8456: Remote Airstrip Upgrade Program – Round 12
grants.summary: The Remote Airstrip Upgrade Program provides grants to enhance the safety and accessibility of aerodromes/airports in remote and very remote areas of Australia. This will: improve the safety of aircraft, operators and passengers using remote and very remote airstrips facilitate improved delivery of essential goods and services such as food supplies, health care, community mail and passenger air services complement air services delivery to communities subsidised under the Australian Government’s Remote Air Services Subsidy (RASS) Scheme meet operational requirements of aeromedical (including the RFDS) and emergency services support improved access to air services for people with disability. Grants will be from $5,000 to $4 million. The grant will be up to 50% of eligible project costs (grant percentage), unless either: the applicant (you) and a third party (could include state, territory or local government or other non-government funding) are both contributing to eligible project costs, the grant amount for this opportunity may be reduced to a third of eligible project costs the applicant (you) meets the definition in the grant opportunity guidelines as an Indigenous Owned and/or Operated Aerodrome, the grant will be up to 100% of eligible project costs.

grants.title: GO8369: Protecting the Great Barrier Reef - Community Stewardship Program Round 2
grants.summary: The Australian Government is inviting applications by an open competitive process to apply to deliver services under the Protecting the Great Barrier Reef — Community Stewardship Program Round 2. The Australian Government announced a total of up to $12.5 million (GST exclusive) over 7 years from 2023–24 to 2029–30 for the Protecting the Great Barrier Reef – Community Stewardship Program. For this grant opportunity (Round 2), up to $7.538 million (GST exclusive) is available over 4 years from 2026–27 to 2029–30. Objectives of the Round 2 grant opportunity are to: deliver community-based, on-ground actions that measurably improve the health and resilience of key Reef species and habitats build a long-lasting inclusive and interconnected community stewardship network that mobilises and coordinates communities, Traditional Owners and partners to protect the Reef. Intended outcomes of the Round 2 grant opportunity are to: contribute to the delivery of the Reef 2050 Plan and at least one of the Reef Trust Outcomes support actions addressing the threats to the Reef’s ecosystem and heritage values associated with climate change, coastal development, land-based runoff and direct use, identified in the Great Barrier Reef Outlook Report 2024 increase community-based protection of the Reef through environmentally responsible practices and strengthen coordination of Reef protection activities by local communities empower local communities, including Traditional Owners, to engage in a culture of stewardship that delivers positive outcomes for the Reef.

grants.title: GO8622: Children's Mobility Capacity
grants.summary: The Australian Government is inviting one organisation via a restricted process to apply to deliver services under the Families and Communities Program – Families and Children Activity – Children and Parenting Support program in the Perth – North West (SA4) area in 2026–27. The FaC Activity aims to support families, strengthen relationships, improve the wellbeing of children and young people and increase participation of people in community life to enhance family and community functioning. The Children and Parent Support program contributes to achieving the objectives of the FaC Activity, and focuses on providing: early intervention and prevention services aimed at improving children’s development and wellbeing adjunct care and early leaning services support to those in a parenting/carer role. The objectives of the grant opportunity are: support the purchase and installation of new CNC machines strengthen Wheelchairs for Kids Australia’s production reliability and operational sustainability. The intended outcomes of the grant opportunity are: increased organisational capacity to manufacture safe, durable and adjustable all-terrain wheelchairs for children with disability continued delivery of wheelchairs at no cost to children and families, improving children’s mobility, dignity, social participation and access to education improved long-term sustainability of the organisation’s manufacturing operations through modernised equipment with reduced maintenance risks.

grants.title: GO8586: Australian Orphanage Museum Operations
grants.summary: The Australian Government is inviting application via a restricted process to apply to deliver services under the Families and Communities – National Find and Connect Program in 2027–28 to 2029–30. The Museum memorialises the history and experiences of approximately 500,000 children who grew up in facilities, such as orphanages, children's homes and foster ‘care’ throughout Australia, up until the end of 1989. The Museum aims to ensure Australians do not forget the past and are reminded of our responsibility to protect all children in our community. The Museum is operated by Care Leavers Australasia Network (CLAN), an independent, peak membership body which provides support, advocacy, research and training for survivors of past abuse in child welfare systems in Australia and New Zealand. This includes former state wards, foster children, and children raised in orphanages and other institutions. The objectives of this grant opportunity are: to support the ongoing operational costs of the Museum to assist CLAN with identifying alternative funding sources to support the viability of the Museum to acknowledge and commemorate the experiences of those Australians who grew up in orphanages, children’s homes and other institutions and foster ‘care’ up until 1989.

grants.title: GO8554: Continuation of viral hepatitis prevention and response measures
grants.summary: The purpose of this grant opportunity is to provide funding to support organisations in the design and delivery of national viral hepatitis community-led initiatives and awareness raising campaigns that engage priority populations, including people at higher risk of acquiring viral hepatitis or with limited access to health care. These activities will help reduce stigma and encourage individuals to seek care and reduce hepatitis-related cancer mortality. This includes: • $6.9 million from 1 January 2027 to 30 June 2029 for National Hepatitis B projects. • $9.0 million 1 January 2027 to 30 June 2029 for National Hepatitis C projects. The objectives of the grant are: • To provide funding to eligible organisations to maintain nationally coordinated activities that improve prevention, testing, diagnosis and treatment outcomes for hepatitis B and C. • To provide funding to eligible organisations to deliver evidence-based activities that address gaps in hepatitis B and C continuum of care. • To address goals and targets in the Strategies. The intended outcomes of the grant opportunity are: • To support harm reduction, public awareness and education, and targeted approaches that increase testing, reduce stigma and discrimination, and strengthen access to culturally safe and appropriate care, particularly among priority populations experiencing inequitable health outcomes. • To reduce hepatitis-related cancer mortality. • To support the national elimination of hepatitis B and C as public health challenges in Australia by 2030. Note: Please see updated Grant Opportunity Guidelines – Version 3 and updated Frequently Asked Questions – Version 2, published on 25 September 2026. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8607: Festivals Australia - Round 23
grants.summary: Festivals Australia provides funding to support individual art projects in regional or remote locations. Eligible projects take place at festivals, or significant one-off community events such as a town celebration or opening of a new community resource. Festivals Australia will: provide access to a diverse range of engaging, innovative arts projects that grow audiences at festivals across regional and remote Australia, support partnerships and collaboration across the arts sector, and encourage community participation in arts projects at regional and remote festivals. The program delivers two funding rounds each year usually opening in February and September. The Minister for the Arts (or their delegate) approves funding under the Program Guidelines. To check if your project is taking place in an eligible location, visit the Festivals Australia Eligibility Map. Enter the full address where your project will be delivered into the search box, or click on the location on the map. The remoteness classification, and whether this location is eligible, will be displayed.

grants.title: GO8382: On Farm Connectivity Program Round 3
grants.summary: The On Farm Connectivity Program Round 3 assists Primary Producers to take advantage of digital agribusiness solutions to boost productivity and improve safety. The grant is provided as a rebate to Approved Suppliers following the sale, delivery, installation, and training, where applicable, of eligible equipment to eligible Primary Producers. Eligible Primary Producers must access the program through an Approved Supplier. The program forms part of the Australian Government’s Better Connectivity Plan for Regional and Rural Australia. To support equitable access to funding, assessments will be prioritised for applications where the Primary Producer has not previously received a benefit under earlier rounds of the On Farm Connectivity Program.

grants.title: GO8589: Comprehensive Primary Health Care – New Entrants
grants.summary: The purpose of this grant opportunity is to provide funding for selected Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Services (ACCHSs), currently delivering General Practitioner services, to provide Comprehensive Primary Health Care (CPHC) under the Indigenous Australians’ Health Programme (IAHP) who have not previously been funded to do so. This funding will be available over four years from 2026-27 to 2029-30. The objectives of the grant opportunity are to: • provide First Nations people with improved access to culturally appropriate comprehensive primary health care services by: Supporting ACCHSs to expand or enhance service availability, service frequency, the range of services offered, workforce capability, service integration and geographic coverage • support ACCHSs to deliver culturally appropriate comprehensive primary health care services tailored to the health needs and priorities of their communities, and • support ACCHSs to embed Continuous Quality Improvement and best practice clinical and organisational governance into CPHC service delivery, supporting good health outcomes for clients and service sustainability. The intended outcomes of the grant opportunity are: • First Nations people can access culturally appropriate CPHC services, where and when they need it • ACCHSs deliver culturally appropriate CPHC services that meet the health needs and priorities of their local communities, and • ACCHSs deliver best practice CPHC services to their local communities. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.
